questions.explanation: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles, so its angle sum is 2 × 180°.

A lower frequency in every case

questions.explanation: Weight = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N.

The bus increases the passenger’s mass

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Two resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A 100 W lamp is used for 5 hours. How much electrical energy does it use?

questions.subject: physics

Along the surface in every case

At the principal focus on the far side

The field becomes a gravitational field

Moving a magnet into the coil

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which statement describes a gas in a closed container?
options: It always settles as a solid layer
It spreads out to fill the available space
It always keeps a fixed shape
It can exist only as bubbles in water
questions.explanation: Gas particles spread throughout the available space.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which mixture can be separated into a solid and a liquid using filter paper?
questions.explanation: Filter paper traps insoluble sand while water passes through.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Muddy water is left undisturbed and heavier solid particles settle. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Sedimentation is the settling of heavier suspended particles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: After sand settles in water, what is decantation?
options: Heating the sand until it melts
Carefully pouring off the clear water
questions.explanation: Decantation separates a liquid by pouring it off without disturbing the settled solid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: In a sugar solution made with water, what is the solvent?
questions.explanation: The solvent is the substance in which the solute dissolves.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: At a fixed temperature, extra salt remains undissolved even after stirring. The solution is likely what?
questions.explanation: A saturated solution cannot dissolve more of that solute at the same temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which process can recover solid salt from salt water by removing the water?
questions.explanation: Water evaporates, leaving the non-volatile dissolved salt behind.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which gas in air supports ordinary burning?
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports the combustion of many common fuels.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which pair of conditions is needed for ordinary rusting of iron?
options: Salt and darkness without air or water
questions.explanation: Iron rusts when it reacts with oxygen in the presence of water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which example is a mixture of two solids?
questions.explanation: Rice and lentils are different solids mixed together.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Oil and water are shaken together and then left to stand. What usually happens?
questions.explanation: Oil and water do not mix uniformly and separate into layers.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which familiar substance is acidic?
questions.explanation: Lemon juice contains citric acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: What does an acid generally do to blue litmus paper?
options: Leaves it blue in every case
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A basic solution generally turns red litmus paper which colour?
questions.explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: An acid reacts with a base in a simple neutralisation reaction. What are the usual products?
questions.explanation: A typical acid-base neutralisation produces a salt and water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which example is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Cutting changes the paper’s size and shape without forming a new substance.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which observation is evidence of a chemical change in an iron nail?
options: The nail is moved to another shelf
The nail is cut into two pieces
The nail is cooled without reacting
questions.explanation: Rust is a new substance formed by the reaction of iron with oxygen and water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Why does an intact paint coating help protect an iron gate from rust?
options: It removes the need for iron
It limits contact with water and oxygen
It changes all the iron into gold
questions.explanation: Paint acts as a barrier between iron and the water and oxygen around it.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which gas turns clear lime water milky?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water to form insoluble calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A concentrated salt solution slowly loses water and forms regular solid crystals. What is this process?
questions.explanation: Crystallisation produces solid crystals from a solution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Turmeric paper turns reddish-brown when touched with which type of solution?
questions.explanation: Turmeric changes from yellow to reddish-brown in a basic solution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which property lets many metals be beaten into thin sheets?
questions.explanation: Malleability is the ability to be shaped into thin sheets.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Why is copper commonly used inside electrical wires?
questions.explanation: Copper allows electric charge to flow easily.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which of these is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Sulphur is a non-metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A fuel must usually reach which temperature before it starts burning in air?
questions.explanation: Ignition temperature is the minimum temperature needed for a substance to catch fire under given conditions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Why is petroleum classified as a non-renewable resource?
options: It is produced instantly by sunlight
It can never be used as fuel
It is made daily by every living plant
It forms far more slowly than we use it
questions.explanation: Petroleum forms over geological timescales and is used much faster than it is replaced.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Coal formed mainly from the remains of what?
questions.explanation: Ancient plant material changed into coal under heat and pressure over very long periods.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Many plastics are made of long molecules containing repeating units. These molecules are called what?
questions.explanation: Polymers are large molecules built from repeating smaller units.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Zinc placed in copper sulphate solution can displace copper because zinc is what?
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive metal from its salt solution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which non-metal conducts electricity and is used in some electrodes?
questions.explanation: Graphite is a form of carbon with electrons that can move through its structure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which poisonous gas can form when a carbon-containing fuel burns with too little oxygen?
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels can produce carbon monoxide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which particle has a positive electric charge?
questions.explanation: A proton carries one positive elementary charge.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: An atom has 8 protons. What is its atomic number?
questions.explanation: Atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A neutral sodium atom contains 11 protons. How many electrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of what?
questions.explanation: Isotopes share an atomic number but have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are represented by one molecule of H₂O?
questions.explanation: The subscript 2 applies to hydrogen, so one water molecule has two hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: In a chemical reaction in a sealed container, total mass before and after the reaction is what?
questions.explanation: Mass is conserved in an ordinary chemical reaction when matter cannot enter or leave.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which sample is a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: A salt solution has a uniform composition throughout.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A beam of light becomes visible as it passes through a colloid. What is this scattering called?
questions.explanation: Colloidal particles scatter light, producing the Tyndall effect.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Compared with a solid, particles in a gas usually have what arrangement?
options: They all occupy the same point
They contain no space between them
They are fixed in a rigid lattice
questions.explanation: Gas particles are widely separated and move freely.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Using H = 1 and O = 16, what is the relative molecular mass of water, H₂O?
questions.explanation: Two hydrogen atoms contribute 2 and one oxygen atom contributes 16, giving 18.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which coefficients correctly balance H₂ + O₂ → H₂O?
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms on each side.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: In CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂, which reaction type is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Two reactants combine to form a single product.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which substance is reduced?
questions.explanation: Copper oxide loses oxygen to form copper, so it is reduced.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which of these pH values represents the most acidic aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: A lower pH indicates a higher hydrogen-ion concentration and greater acidity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Sodium chloride forms mainly through which process?
options: Conversion of sodium nuclei into chlorine nuclei
Transfer of an electron from sodium to chlorine
Equal sharing of all sodium electrons
Transfer of a proton from chlorine to sodium
questions.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine, forming oppositely charged ions that attract.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: What is the molecular formula of methane?
questions.explanation: Methane has one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Successive members of an alkane homologous series differ by which group?
questions.explanation: Consecutive alkanes differ by one carbon and two hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form zinc chloride and which gas?
questions.explanation: Zinc displaces hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Why does soap form scum in hard water?
options: It reacts with calcium and magnesium ions to form insoluble salts
It changes all the water into oil
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions form insoluble salts with soap.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: During electrolysis of water, the volume of hydrogen collected is approximately how many times the volume of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Water produces hydrogen and oxygen in a volume ratio of 2:1.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which part usually anchors a plant in the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots hold a plant in place and absorb water and minerals.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which part of a bean plant can grow into a new bean plant under suitable conditions?
questions.explanation: A seed contains a young plant that can grow when conditions are suitable.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which animal is a herbivore?
questions.explanation: A cow mainly eats plant material.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which organ is mainly used to hear sounds?
questions.explanation: Ears detect sounds.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which body parts form the main framework that supports the human body?
questions.explanation: Bones form the skeleton, which supports and protects the body.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which energy source do green plants use to make food?
questions.explanation: Green plants use light energy during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which organs do people mainly use to take oxygen from the air?
questions.explanation: The lungs exchange gases between the air and the blood.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which animal is naturally adapted to living mainly in water?
questions.explanation: Fish have adaptations such as gills that help them live in water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which is a usual sign that a healthy young plant is growing?
questions.explanation: Producing new leaves is one sign of plant growth.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Why do humans need food?
options: To obtain energy and materials for growth
questions.explanation: Food supplies energy and nutrients needed for growth and repair.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which set of conditions is needed by most seeds to begin germinating?
options: Only dry soil and no air
Water, oxygen and a suitable temperature
Only bright light and no water
questions.explanation: Most seeds need water, oxygen and a suitable temperature to germinate.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which gas do green plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water to make food during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is pollination?
options: Transfer of pollen to the stigma of a flower
Loss of water from a leaf
questions.explanation: Pollination transfers pollen from an anther to a stigma.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In the chain grass → grasshopper → frog, which organism eats the grasshopper?
questions.explanation: The arrow shows food passing from the grasshopper to the frog.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
questions.explanation: The heart contracts to pump blood through blood vessels.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which bones protect the brain?
questions.explanation: The skull forms a protective case around the brain.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which organisms help break down dead leaves into simpler substances?
questions.explanation: Decomposers recycle materials by breaking down dead organic matter.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is stored mainly in a camel’s hump?
questions.explanation: A camel’s hump stores fat, which can be used as an energy reserve.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which stage comes between a caterpillar and an adult butterfly?
questions.explanation: A caterpillar changes into a pupa before becoming an adult butterfly.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which meal is most likely to provide a wider range of nutrients?
options: Only plain rice at every meal
questions.explanation: A variety of foods provides different nutrients needed by the body.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which plant part usually carries water between the roots and leaves?
questions.explanation: Water travels from the roots through the stem toward the leaves.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which plant commonly has a fibrous root system?
questions.explanation: Wheat has many thin roots arising near the base of its stem.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What are stomata?
options: Tiny pores on plant surfaces, especially leaves
questions.explanation: Stomata are pores involved in gas exchange and water-vapour loss.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which animal has no backbone?
questions.explanation: An earthworm is an invertebrate, meaning it lacks a backbone.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: An organism’s habitat is best described as what?
options: The number of legs it has
The place where it naturally lives
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural place where an organism lives.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which type of joint mainly allows your elbow to bend and straighten?
questions.explanation: A hinge joint allows movement mainly in one plane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which nutrient is especially important for growth and repair of body tissues?
questions.explanation: Proteins provide building material for growth and tissue repair.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is one main role of dietary fibre?
options: Carrying oxygen in red blood cells
Helping food waste move through the gut
Replacing all protein in the body
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre adds bulk and helps the movement of waste through the intestine.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: A touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. Which feature of living things does this show?
questions.explanation: Touch is a stimulus, and leaf folding is the plant’s response.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is the loss of water vapour from plant leaves called?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly leaves.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed in humans?
questions.explanation: The small intestine has a large surface area for nutrient absorption.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which food component starts to be chemically digested by an enzyme in saliva?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase begins breaking down starch.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Respiration releases energy from food molecules for cellular activities.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In human lungs, where does most gas exchange take place?
questions.explanation: Alveoli have thin walls and a large surface area for gas exchange.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, regardless of its oxygen content.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which plant tissue mainly carries water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots?
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: A potato tuber can produce a new plant from its buds. This is an example of what?
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation produces a new plant from a vegetative part of the parent.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which human organs filter blood and form urine?
questions.explanation: Kidneys remove wastes and excess water from the blood to form urine.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In a lichen, which partner usually makes food by photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The photosynthetic partner provides food, while the fungus offers protection and support.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: When do living plant cells carry out respiration?
options: Both during the day and at night
questions.explanation: Living plant cells need energy and respire throughout the day and night.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which structure controls most activities of a typical animal cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains genetic material and helps control cell activities.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which structure is present in typical green leaf cells but absent from animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which microorganism is commonly used to make bread dough rise?
questions.explanation: Yeast releases carbon dioxide during fermentation, making dough rise.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Rhizobium bacteria in legume root nodules help plants by doing what?
options: Converting atmospheric nitrogen into usable nitrogen compounds
Removing every mineral from the soil
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen into forms that can support plant growth.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is fertilisation?
options: Fusion of male and female gametes
questions.explanation: Fertilisation joins male and female gametes to form a zygote.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Where does a human embryo normally develop after implantation?
questions.explanation: The embryo normally implants and develops in the uterus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which animal undergoes a change from tadpole to adult?
questions.explanation: A frog develops from a tadpole through metamorphosis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In humans, hormones are best described as what?
options: Chemical messengers produced by endocrine glands
questions.explanation: Hormones carry signals that help regulate body functions.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: An endemic species is one that is what?
options: Naturally found only in a particular region
questions.explanation: An endemic species has a natural distribution restricted to a particular region.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is a main function of the cell membrane?
options: Replacing the nucleus in every cell
Regulating the movement of substances into and out of the cell
Storing all food outside the cell
questions.explanation: The cell membrane selectively regulates exchange with the surroundings.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which organelle is a major site of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out key stages of aerobic respiration and produce ATP.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is osmosis?
options: Movement of solid particles by a magnet
Net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from a more dilute solution to a more concentrated solution
Movement of only large proteins through a metal sheet
questions.explanation: In osmosis, water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from a more dilute solution to a more concentrated one.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which tissue contains actively dividing cells that help a plant grow?
questions.explanation: Meristematic cells divide to produce new cells for plant growth.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which tissue transmits electrical signals around the body?
questions.explanation: Neurons in nervous tissue carry electrical signals.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is a tissue?
options: A group of cells working together to perform a function
questions.explanation: A tissue is an organised group of cells performing a particular function.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which feature is typical of a bacterial cell?
options: It has a large chloroplast in every case
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes with genetic material that is not enclosed in a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which blood cells mainly transport oxygen?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which carries oxygen.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which process returns carbon dioxide to the atmosphere from living organisms?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration releases carbon dioxide when organic food molecules are broken down aerobically.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Chromosomes are composed mainly of DNA and what other type of molecule?
questions.explanation: Chromosomal DNA is associated with proteins that help package and organise it.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: A cell placed in a very concentrated salt solution loses water. What happens to the water?
options: It is all destroyed by the salt
questions.explanation: The more concentrated external solution draws water out through the cell membrane by osmosis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which raw materials are used to make glucose during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water, with light energy, to form carbohydrates.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Bile helps fat digestion mainly by doing what?
options: Breaking large fat droplets into smaller droplets
Digesting proteins into amino acids directly
questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies fats, increasing the surface area available to digestive enzymes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Why is human circulation called double circulation?
options: The heart has only two chambers
Every artery contains two separate hearts
Blood flows only twice each day
Blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit
questions.explanation: The pulmonary and systemic circuits together take blood through the heart twice.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is the basic functional unit of a human kidney?
questions.explanation: Nephrons filter blood and modify the filtrate to form urine.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which structure usually coordinates a simple spinal withdrawal reflex?
questions.explanation: A spinal reflex is coordinated through the spinal cord for a rapid response.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which plant hormone promotes cell elongation and helps a shoot bend toward light?
questions.explanation: Uneven auxin distribution causes unequal elongation on the two sides of a shoot.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In a simple Mendelian cross, Tt × Tt, what fraction of offspring is expected to be tt?
questions.explanation: The four equally likely combinations are TT, Tt, Tt and tt.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Why does sexual reproduction usually produce more genetic variation than asexual reproduction?
options: DNA is absent from the offspring
Genetic material from two parents is combined
All offspring receive identical copies from one parent
questions.explanation: Combining parental genetic material creates new combinations of inherited variants.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Why is less energy generally available at higher trophic levels?
options: Consumers return all energy to sunlight
Organisms use energy and much is released as heat at each level
Energy is created only by carnivores
All energy is recycled without any losses
questions.explanation: Energy is used in life processes and dissipated as heat, so only part reaches the next level.

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which material is readily biodegradable under suitable conditions?
questions.explanation: Microorganisms can break down vegetable peels into simpler substances.
